summary: I've been lucky enough to work across some of France's most demanding broadcast and adtech environments, **TF1, Mediawan, Equativ**, each one raising the bar on what production-grade actually means.
I bring full-stack depth across Angular, .NET, and cloud infrastructure, and the ability to walk into a complex codebase and make it better for the team around me.

In 2026, when AI tooling landed on our team, I took on the AI engineering side as well: building agent skills and MCP servers, reviewing AI-generated code, and helping the team get real use out of it. On my own time, I am building an autonomous agent project.

experience.summary: Maintaining and modernising a dense internal ecosystem, and helping the team get real use out of AI tooling.

highlights.text: Maintained and improved 6 existing projects, some more than 9 years old, and delivered 2 new applications built on the legacy codebase.
Worked inside a dense internal ecosystem (a custom translation app, a settings app, in-house JavaScript libraries), where understanding how everything connects is a job in itself.
Became the person the team calls to unblock failing test environments, which means debugging across several services.
Wrote coding conventions and architecture guidelines to modernise the team's engineering practices.
When AI tooling was rolled out company-wide in 2026, helped the team adopt it, with suggestions on how to structure Jira tickets and practical guidelines.
Proposed and built internal MCP servers and agent skills, so the AI tooling has the context it needs to work in our codebase.
Used AI agents on complex cases that cut across several services and years of legacy code.
Reviewed AI-generated contributions for security gaps and design issues before they pile up.

experience.summary: Engineering services company (ESN). Two client missions, TF1 then Mediawan, alongside responsibilities for OMNILOG itself.

highlights.text: Trained and mentored other OMNILOG engineers.
Carried out technical assessments on behalf of OMNILOG.
Discussed the scope and direction of my roles directly with client management.
Designed and built an internal automation platform from scratch, on my own, which cut the team's manual back-end work.
Ran the Agile ceremonies and internal training sessions.
Became the person to ask about difficult back-end problems.

experience.role: Fullstack Dev, Lead Tech, Front Expert

highlights.text: Rewrote the core ad engine of the TF1 group, a monolith that runs every night, moving it from a legacy desktop application to a web platform.
Built a single Design System for the ad department.
Ran Coding Kata workshops to bring 10 to 15 engineers up to speed on Angular.
Kept product managers, product owners and developers aligned, settled disagreements and set the technical guardrails.
Delivered 6 applications to production: 5 internal and 1 external.
Picked up a project nobody on the team wanted, evaluated the Blazor framework and presented the findings to more than 30 .NET engineers.
Contributed to 2 major projects: EsiGate and the Electron framework.
As an intern, modernised internal software that the full-time developers had not had time for. It taught me that treating every task as if it matters is the simplest way to earn a team's trust.
